subject.title: [Feature]: Add provider-profile routing policies for multi-account OAuth/API pools (starting with google-gemini-cli)

question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in provider-profile pool routing contract for batch/worker workloads, and what minimal config, state, and status surface should ship first?
rationale: The remaining work changes public config, persisted auth state, provider fallback semantics, status/probe output, provider/plugin ownership, and upgrade behavior, so automation should not invent the product boundary or defaults.

options.title: Design minimal additive core pool routing
options.body: Preserve current session-sticky defaults and start with one opt-in, observable provider/auth pool strategy before expanding into quota, bucket, weight, and cost semantics.

options.title: Track narrower primitives first
options.body: Keep this as the umbrella while #28847, #79604, and #45771 define smaller quota-bucket, rotation-depth, and pace-governance acceptance criteria.

options.title: Defer to external/plugin surfaces
options.body: Keep current core behavior and recommend sidecars or future provider/plugin hooks until maintainers decide native config and state complexity is justified.

recommendation.title: Design minimal additive core pool routing
recommendation.body: Preserve current session-sticky defaults and start with one opt-in, observable provider/auth pool strategy before expanding into quota, bucket, weight, and cost semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision crosses auth config, persisted state, provider routing, docs, and compatibility policy, and steipete has the strongest recent history on those boundaries.
